findings.explanation: 1897 is the deprecated 'Cisco ACI Add-on for Splunk Enterprise' (listing says migrate to 7777) and the cached catalogue refers to 4241 as the 'VMware NSX-T Splunk App'; neither they nor the VMware add-on 3215 produce any of the five sourcetypes the SPL reads.
findings.quote: **Splunk Add-on for Cisco ACI** ([Splunkbase 1897](https://splunkbase.splunk.com/app/1897)); **Splunk Add-on for VMware NSX** ([Splunkbase 4241](https://splunkbase.splunk.com/app/4241))
findings.suggested_fix: Remove 1897/4241/3215 from app, dataSources and references, or move them to an optional correlation note with correct names.

findings.explanation: `show system resources` is an NX-OS command; EOS reports CPU/memory through other commands (e.g. process/top and version output), so the instruction may not work as written.
findings.quote: Map **Arista EOS** **show system resources** and platform forwarding-capacity output into the same **cpu_pct**, **mem_used_pct**
findings.suggested_fix: Check the Arista EOS command reference and name the EOS commands that expose CPU, memory and forwarding-table capacity.

findings.explanation: The SPL's cpu_pct coalesce includes kernel_percent, which is only the kernel share of CPU in `show system resources`; busy% is 100 minus idle. The guidance and the fallback field disagree.
findings.quote: Emit **cpu_pct** as worst-case supervisor busy% and **mem_used_pct** from total memory counters
findings.suggested_fix: State that collectors must emit cpu_pct = 100 - idle, and note that kernel_percent alone underestimates load.

findings.explanation: Performance (CPU/Memory datasets) is a reasonable fit for switch CPU/memory, but the SPL is a raw search with no field mapping, FIB/TCAM utilisation has no CIM home, and Alerts/Inventory are not exercised.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep Performance only if CPU/Memory fields are mapped to the CIM names, and drop Inventory/Alerts unless mappings are documented.

findings.explanation: The URL is the Cisco.com home page, not the named guide; the Arista link is the generic EOS manual root.
findings.quote:
"title": "Cisco Nexus 9000 Series NX-OS System Management Configuration Guide, Release 10.3.x",
      "url": "https://www.cisco.com/c/en/us/"
findings.suggested_fix: Link the actual NX-OS System Management guide page and the EOS manual section for hardware capacity/resource commands.

findings.explanation: The closing code fence is glued to the last SPL line, so markdown renderers may not close the block and copy-paste can include the backticks.
findings.quote: | table _time leaf cpu_peak mem_peak fib_util_peak tcam_util_peak fib_used_latest fib_cap tcam_used_latest tcam_cap score_peak st_seen story```
findings.suggested_fix: Put the closing ``` on its own line.

findings.explanation: Marked verified by an automated reviewer with no SME sign-off while add-on facts are wrong.

firewalled_field_flags.issue: cpu_pct falls back to kernel_percent, which in NX-OS `show system resources` is only the kernel share; leaves with high user-space CPU can be under-reported and miss the 85% threshold.

summary: One of the stronger siblings: the SPL is coherent, thresholds in prose match the code, and validation/troubleshooting steps are concrete. It is let down by the recurring mis-named and irrelevant ACI/NSX/VMware add-ons, a placeholder Cisco reference, and a few unverified platform/CLI claims.
